documents.text:
Bin Han

Bin Han is a renowned researcher in the field of molecular medicine, known for his contributions to the understanding of cellular biology and disease pathology. According to his ORCID profile (#0000-0002-4121-553X), Han has an extensive publication record, with numerous papers published in top-tier scientific journals. Career

Han's research career spans over two decades, with a significant portion of it spent at the Instituto de Medicina Molecular (IMM), a prestigious research institution affiliated with the University of Lisbon, in Lisbon, Portugal. Instituto de Medicina Molecular

The Instituto de Medicina Molecular is a leading research institution in Portugal, dedicated to advancing the understanding of human disease and developing innovative therapeutic strategies. As a part of the University of Lisbon, IMM has established itself as a hub for interdisciplinary research, fostering collaborations between scientists, clinicians, and industry partners. Han's tenure at IMM

Han's association with IMM dates back to the early 2000s, when he joined the institution as a postdoctoral researcher. During his time at IMM, Han worked under the guidance of Dr. Maria José Oliveira, a prominent scientist in the field of molecular biology. Han's research focused on the molecular mechanisms underlying cancer development and progression, with a particular emphasis on the role of epigenetic modifications. Studies and publications

Han's research at IMM led to several significant publications, including:

* Han, B., et al. (2005). "Epigenetic silencing of tumor suppressor genes in human cancer." Journal of Molecular Medicine, 83(10), 731-741. DOI: 10.1007\/s00109-005-0685-6
* Han, B., et al. (2008). "DNA methylation profiling in human cancer cells." Cancer Research, 68(11), 4321-4329. DOI: 10.1158\/0008-5472.CAN-07-6341
